monthly_review.summary: Pace improved sharply (+25 sec/km faster) and efficiency declined slightly, but zone distribution shifted dramatically toward higher intensities — a sign of accumulated fatigue masking fitness gains.
monthly_review.highlight: Despite a 25-sec/km pace improvement, aerobic decoupling rose (+0.3%) and running economy worsened (+0.44 ml/kg/km) — indicating compromised efficiency at same effort, consistent with fatigue rather than true adaptation.

goal_tracker.message: Distance and session count are already matched with last month — but given compromised readiness, adding any extra volume or intensity in the remaining 10 days is inadvisable. Rest and consolidation are the priority.

insights.title: Zone shift reveals fatigue-driven pacing distortion
insights.body: Z3–Z4 time jumped from 34% (Aug: 26%+8%) to 51% (Sep: 29%+22%), while Z1 collapsed from 43% to 22% — yet average HR rose 6 bpm and aerobic TE worsened. This suggests compensatory effort, not intentional threshold work.

insights.title: Cadence drop correlates with efficiency decline
insights.body: Cadence fell from 149 spm (Aug) to 142 spm (Sep), matching the rise in running economy (worsening) from 14.12 to 14.56 ml/kg/km — lower turnover often reflects reduced neuromuscular freshness or altered gait under fatigue.

insights.title: Aerobic decoupling increase despite slower long run pace
insights.body: Sept 6 long run was 12:22/km (722 sec/km) at 158 bpm — very slow but elicited 5.0% aerobic TE, the highest in all recent runs; contrast with July’s 14.8 km at 518 sec/km (8:38/km) and only 2.9% TE. Fatigue is degrading aerobic resilience even at low intensities.

insights.title: Missing HRV and sleep data prevents objective readiness confirmation
insights.body: No HRV, resting HR trend, or sleep metrics are present — yet avg HR rose and efficiency declined, implying unmeasured autonomic strain. This data gap makes readiness assessment inherently conservative.

recommendations.action: Zone 1–2 run, HR ≤130 bpm, 45 min easy on Tuesday
recommendations.reason: To actively lower sympathetic tone and support parasympathetic rebound amid elevated avg HR and suppressed efficiency

recommendations.action: Complete 2 full rest days (no movement beyond walking) before Saturday

recommendations.action: Evening 10-min guided breathing (4-7-8 protocol) for 7 consecutive nights
recommendations.reason: Compensates for missing HRV data by directly targeting vagal tone; paired with elevated avg HR and rising aerobic TE, this supports autonomic recalibration

risk_flags.evidence: Avg HR +6 bpm, aerobic TE +0.3%, efficiency +0.44 ml/kg/km, Z1 time halved (43% → 22%), no HRV or resting HR trend
risk_flags.action: Pause all Z3+ work for 7 days; re-evaluate after 3 days of Zone 1 and rest

risk_flags.evidence: Cadence down 7 spm, ground contact time increased (e.g., Sept 6: 327 ms vs Aug median ~300 ms implied by stride/cadence), vertical oscillation up to 9.2 cm on short 1.0 km sprint
risk_flags.action: Avoid strides or fast finishes until cadence stabilises ≥146 spm for 3 consecutive runs
